sources.mellor: Anne K. Mellor, "Revising Frankenstein," ch. 9 of Mary Shelley: Her Life, Her Fiction, Her Monsters (New York: Routledge, 1988); argues the 1831 text makes Victor the pawn of a destiny beyond his control. Online at https://knarf.english.upenn.edu/Articles/mellor9.html (refused automated access on 2026-11-03; the claim summarized here was confirmed against the texts by this step, not against Mellor's page).
sources.curran: Stuart Curran, ed., Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, Romantic Circles Electronic Editions (2009), annotation at https://romantic-circles.org/editions/frankenstein/1065.html: in 1831 "I believed myself destined" is substituted for "I felt as if I were destined", and Victor "has consistently appealed to a ruling destiny" already in 1818.
sources.intro: Mary Shelley, Introduction to the 1831 edition (in inputs/pg42324.txt): the revisions "are principally those of style. I have changed no portion of the story, nor introduced any new ideas or circumstances."
sources.wikiLavenza: Wikipedia, "Elizabeth Lavenza," https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Lavenza (consulted 2026-11-03; a tertiary source that cites no scholarship for the claim, listed so students can see the difference).
sources.texts: The two editions themselves (inputs/pg41445.txt and inputs/pg42324.txt). Commonly noted in teaching editions; no scholarly source was checked in the time available.

shelleyClaim.method: Words changed (the larger of words added and words removed) in every non-punctuation change, excluding the new Introduction. "Beginning of the first volume" = the four letters and Vol. I, Chs. I–II of 1818.
